text:
rachel: Quick heads-up — starting a staged rollout for the quant-kernel bundle (qkernel-1.4.0) at 02:00 UTC. This is a small change: matmul kernel variant + improved fp16 path. Will do region-by-region canary, then 10% -> 50% -> 100%.

rachel: Plan is to smoke in us-east-1, then eu-west-1, then ap-southeast-1. Keeping the old kernel pinned for critical customers during the 2h window.

deploy-bot: [automated] initiating canary rollout qkernel-1.4.0 -> us-east-1 (10% traffic). Change window: 02:00-04:00 UTC. Rollout id: rb-1934567890.

omar: FYI: the older A100 images in eu-west-1 had a driver mismatch last time. Recommend pinning eu-west-1 default to qkernel-1.3.8 for now and only flip for customers that opt-in.

sylvia: +1 on opt-in only. Also add this quick smoke: run `python tools/smoke_infer.py --model gpt-medium --seq 512 --batch 1 --quant` against canary host. Check loss drift <0.5% and p95 latency not increased by >10%.

kevin: Rollback criteria proposal: auto-rollback if error rate increases >0.5% absolute or latency p95 increases >20% for 3 consecutive 1-min buckets. Manual rollback if any correctness eval fails on our regression set (see internal link).

rachel: Good. Add an extra gate: if tokenization mismatch appears in any customer logs, immediate hold and escalate. That was the surprise last patch.

deploy-bot: [automated] telemetry hooks enabled: perf-streaming, anomaly-detector, trace-sampler=0.1. Will post updates in this thread.

sylvia: I'm going to run the smoke script now against the canary host and post results. Pasting quick command and expected grep:
```
# smoke
python tools/smoke_infer.py --host canary-us-east-1.redwood.internal --model gpt-medium --seq 512 --batch 1 --quant > /tmp/smoke.out
grep "loss:" /tmp/smoke.out && grep "p95:" /tmp/smoke.out
```

sylvia: smoke results: loss: 2.031 -> baseline 2.024 (0.35% drift); p95: 48ms -> baseline 45ms (6.7% increase). Nothing alarming. :thumbsup:

omar: I still want eu-west pinned. Can we flip a test customer (acct: acme-inc) to the canary for 1 hour and watch logs?

rachel: @omar yes — will add acme-inc to opt-in list and route them to canary for an hour starting at 02:15 UTC.

kevin: I'll be on-call 02:00-04:30 to watch the metrics and handle rollback if thresholds hit. If we rollback, plan is: 1) pin traffic back to qkernel-1.3.8, 2) capture full traces, 3) create an incident stub and notify eng-runtime + SRE.

rachel: Release note blurb for the docs page: "qkernel-1.4.0: matmul kernel variant with improved fp16 throughput and reduced memory pressure; recommended for workloads with seq <= 1024. See internal changelog: https://redwood.internal/release/qkernel-1.4.0"

deploy-bot: [automated] update: canary succeeded initial checks (2m snapshot). No error spike. Next step: increase to 50% in us-east-1 at 02:25 UTC.

sylvia: leaving a small runbook snippet here for anyone following:
- How to pin a region: `./tools/pin_kernel --region eu-west-1 --kernel qkernel-1.3.8`
- How to force rollback: `./tools/rollback_rollout rb-1934567890 --force`
- Where to find traces: `https://telemetry.redwood.internal/traces?rollout=rb-1934567890`

omar: Thanks — this looks good. I'll keep an eye on device-side OOM counters. If OOM rate >0 for any host, ping for immediate rollback.

kevin: Noted. Will escalate to infra if we see any kernel panics.

rachel: OK team, let's proceed. Post any anomalies here. I'll file the postmortem template if we need it.

deploy-bot: [automated] 02:26 UTC — rollout increased to 50% (us-east-1). Monitoring...

sylvia: quick note for release notes: include the compatibility caveat about older ROCm drivers. I added that to the docs page.

rachel: Closing the loop: if no regressions by 03:30 UTC, we'll schedule full rollout to remaining regions at 04:00 UTC.

kevin: Acknowledged. I'll leave a Zoom open for 02:00-04:30 if anyone needs ad-hoc discussion.

sylvia: Thanks everyone. :party_parrot:
